name: HDL
definition: Hardware description language: the language, such as Verilog, in which a designer writes a circuit~\cite{jamiesonthesis}.

name: RTL
definition: Register-transfer level: the HDL text that says what the registers hold and how they change~\cite{jamiesonthesis}.

name: gate
definition: A basic logic element (AND, OR, NOT); the elaborated design is first written with such primitive gates~\cite{jamiesonthesis}.

name: netlist
definition: The list of the basic blocks of a design and the nets (wires) that join them; every net is driven by exactly one block~\cite{luuthesis}.

name: flip-flop
definition: A one-bit storage element that keeps its value between clock edges.

name: LUT
definition: Look-up table: a small memory that implements any logic function of $K$ inputs ($K=6$ here). In most FPGAs a LUT and a flip-flop form one basic logic element~\cite{jamiesonthesis}~\cite{luuthesis}.

name: technology mapping
definition: The CAD step that covers the logic of a netlist with the cells the target offers: gates for a gate library, LUTs and flip-flops for an FPGA~\cite{jamiesonthesis}.

name: provenance
definition: The link from each netlist object back to the HDL that produced it.

name: Odin III
definition: The provenance-tracked synthesis front end under Loki; it keeps that link in one intermediate representation.

name: answer key / ground truth
definition: What the synthesis tool recorded about which netlist objects form which HDL construct; the target that recovery is scored against.

name: Gate-Breaker
definition: An earlier study in which a language model rewrites gate netlists into RTL; Loki's method baseline.

name: hypothesis
definition: A claim that an experiment can confirm or fail to confirm. In L1 a structure hypothesis is the claim that a set of netlist cells is a structure of some kind (register, adder, mux, ...).

name: L0 / L1 / L2
definition: Loki's three layers: L0 labelled datasets, L1 a Bayesian flow over structure hypotheses, L2 graph analysis.

name: quartile
definition: One quarter of the benchmark designs ordered by Gate-Breaker's complexity score (Q1 simplest, Q4 most complex).

name: AST / CFG similarity
definition: How alike two RTL texts are by subtree overlap of the syntax trees (AST) and by a kernel on the control-flow graphs (CFG); Gate-Breaker's measures of a recovered text against its reference.

name: micro designs
definition: The 68 small synthesizable RTL designs (counters, registers, arithmetic, ALUs, muxes, comparators, small state machines) used as the first benchmark.

name: VerilogEval references
definition: The 156 reference RTL designs of the VerilogEval spec-to-RTL set; the second benchmark.

name: floor
definition: The abstraction level and technology mapping at which a design is cut and written as the netlist to reconstruct (f1-k6, f1-earch, f2, f3).

name: renamed-instance protocol
definition: Rename every identifier through one shared permutation, run the pipeline, map the tokens back: equal results show that the pipeline does not use names.

name: detector
definition: A plug-in that proposes structure hypotheses for a netlist and reports features of them, never a likelihood.

name: calibration
definition: Fitting priors and likelihood ratios on a training split so that predicted probabilities match observed rates.

name: ECE
definition: Expected calibration error: the average gap between predicted probability and observed match rate over ten bins.

name: prover
definition: An engine (cone check, truth table, transfer) that proves a structure hypothesis equal to the netlist; a proof makes it near certain.

name: count / match (scoring)
definition: A hypothesis is counted when it is committed or has probability at least 0.5; it matches an answer-key instance by an overlap rule (Section~\ref{sec:eval}).

name: precision / recall / F1
definition: Precision is the share of counted hypotheses that match; recall is the share of answer-key instances matched; F1 is their harmonic mean.

name: macro-F1 / micro-F1
definition: F1 averaged over the kinds of structure (macro) or pooled over all instances (micro).

name: Louvain / modularity / NMI
definition: Louvain is a community-detection method; modularity scores how dense the clusters are; NMI scores the agreement of a clustering with the known module hierarchy.

name: GNN and 1-WL baseline
definition: A graph neural network (GNN) labels each netlist node from its neighbours; the 1-WL baseline is colour refinement, whose distinguishing power a message-passing GNN cannot exceed.

name: word
definition: A group of cells that act as one multi-bit signal (a register, a datapath operator, a bus).

name: operator type-F1
definition: F1 of the recovered word-level operator types (adder, mux, comparator, ...) against the answer key's operators.

name: fragment
definition: A wrong-looking candidate that is in fact part of a real construct.

name: word-first detector
definition: A detector that first groups flip-flops into register words by shared clock, enable and reset, then builds the rest around them.

name: DANA (through HAL)
definition: A published method, run through the HAL framework, that groups flip-flops into register words from their shared control nets and the dataflow between them.

name: McNemar / Wilcoxon test
definition: An exact paired test on discordant pairs; a paired rank test.

name: synthetic corpus
definition: A seeded generator's 1200 labelled idiom designs (twelve families) with train, iid and ood splits.

name: signature dictionary
definition: A table from a cell's cone class and WL colour to the construct it usually is, mined from the synthetic corpus.

name: D14 provenance map
definition: Odin III's version-2 name map: per object, the source-statement units it blends, and labelled join records.

name: unit, separable, lost
definition: A unit is the statement-level anchor of a construct; it is separable while some object has exactly that unit set, and lost at the first later snapshot where none has.

name: random-set null / persistence null
definition: The random-set null draws random unit sets of the real sizes at each pass; the persistence null starts from the objects of the previous snapshot and merges at random until the real object count is reached.

name: LLM pilot arms A, B, C
definition: Arm A: gate netlist; arm B: netlist plus Loki hints; arm C: interface line only (memorisation control).
